subject: Acme trial - procurement & commercial path (PO vs card vs marketplace)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme trial - procurement & commercial path (PO vs card vs marketplace)

Thanks again for a great call today, Jennifer - quick recap and next steps.

Summary / context:
- We kicked off Acme's 2-week evaluation for the Redwood inference trial (team: search infra + ML).
- Primary success criteria discussed: end-to-end indexing + embeddings for 5M docs, sub-200ms embedding latency, and end-to-end query accuracy on the benchmarks you shared.

Open / ask for procurement path:
1) How would Acme prefer to handle billing once you move from trial to paid? Options we typically see:
   - Purchase Order (PO) + invoice (standard for enterprise procurement)
   - Corporate card (fastest for short pilots / low-dollar evaluations)
   - Cloud marketplace (AWS Marketplace) - if you want consolidated billing via your marketplace account
2) If PO is preferred, can you share the contact and an expected timeline for issuing the PO?

Operational next steps (what I'll do):
- Attach: trial checklist (trial success criteria + who owns what) - I'll send a formal quote and a sample PO-friendly invoice template.
- If you want to go card-first I can enable billing immediately and we'll convert to PO later if needed.

Proposed timeline: please let me know procurement preference by Thu, Jul 8 so we can avoid any billing gap (trial ends proposed: Thu, Jul 22). If PO timing looks longer we can pause billing until PO effective date.

Thanks - I'll follow up with a short quote/SOW once I have procurement preference.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: redwood_trial_checklist.docx

From: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Collins <peter.collins@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial - procurement & commercial path (PO vs card vs marketplace)

Thanks Marissa - great recap. A few notes from procurement and our side:

- Procurement preference: PO for any vendor engagement expected to exceed ~$10k. For short evaluations under $5k we can accept a corporate card.
- Marketplace: we don't currently centralize through AWS Marketplace for this category, so that path would add ~2 weeks to setup.
- Our procurement contact is Peter Collins (peter.collins@acme.com) - I've cc'd him. He'll need your quote, T&Cs, and our standard vendor form filled.
- Timeline: Peter indicated ~10 business days to issue a PO once he has the quote + vendor form completed; expedited routing is possible for small invoices (< $15k).

I'll also send your procurement team the vendor onboarding form as an attachment.

-- Jennifer
Head of Product, Search
Jennifer.Lee@acme.com

Attachment: Acme_Vendor_Form.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@acme.com>, Peter Collins <peter.collins@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial - procurement & commercial path (PO vs card vs marketplace)

Appreciate the details, Jennifer - and hi Peter, nice to meet you. Quick follow-up with options and what we need from your side to keep the trial -> paid path smooth: 

Commercial options (we can support all three):
A) PO + invoice: we'll send a quote and PO-friendly invoice. If you send the PO number and billing/legal entity + remit address, we'll create the invoice and hold billing to the PO effective date if that's helpful.
B) Corporate card: fastest to start (immediate). We'll require a billing contact and card on file; we can convert the card to a credit against the first PO if you later issue one.
C) Marketplace: if you prefer AWS Marketplace, we can submit the listing, but expect a ~2-week procurement/admin step on your side.

Questions for Acme to confirm conversion readiness (so we can align sales/legal/finance):
- What internal usage threshold would you consider a signal to move to paid? (e.g., X API tokens / Y embeddings / number of production calls)
- Any required success metrics beyond latency and indexing that the business / procurement will use to greenlight a purchase?
- Is SSO / SCIM required before procurement signs? If so we'll prioritize that integration.

Next steps (what I'll send by EOD Fri):
- Formal quote + sample PO invoice (PDF)
- Completed vendor form for Acme to review
- Short SOW referencing the trial success criteria we discussed

If you confirm PO is the preferred path, please send the PO contact info (billing entity, tax ID if needed) and an estimated issuance date.

Thanks - I’ll mark Jul 8 as a decision checkpoint to avoid billing overlap.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments in follow-up: Redwood-Quote-ACME-07012026.pdf

From: Peter Collins <peter.collins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial - procurement & commercial path (PO vs card vs marketplace)

Hi Marissa - thanks. A few procurement clarifications from my side: 

- We will issue a PO for this engagement. Expected timeline: ~10 business days after we receive a complete quote + vendor form.
- For expedited routing (internal approval), invoices under $15k can be fast-tracked - please include a clear line-item total on the quote.
- Required: completed vendor form (attached), our standard PO template (attached) - please populate remit address and tax information.
- Success criteria: product team wants to see (1) embeddings for 5M docs processed during the trial, (2) average embedding latency <= 200ms, (3) successful SSO integration into dev environment.

If you can get the quote + vendor form back to us by Mon, Jul 13 we should be able to get the PO in time to avoid any billing gap.

Thanks,
Peter Collins
Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

Attachments: Acme_PO_Template.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Collins <peter.collins@acme.com>, Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial - procurement & commercial path (PO vs card vs marketplace)

Thanks Peter - appreciate the clear timeline and the template. Quick summary of agreed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

1) Redwood will send:
   - Formal quote & line-item invoice (Redwood-Quote-ACME-07012026.pdf) - includes an option for card or PO billing and a note about pausing billing until PO effective date if requested.
   - Completed vendor form populated with remit & tax info.
   - Short SOW that maps trial success criteria to deliverables and owners.
2) Acme procurement to review vendor form + quote and issue PO (target: within ~10 business days after receipt). For expedited approval, keep line-item total < $15k if possible.
3) Trial success criteria (per product + procurement): 5M docs ingested, avg embedding latency <= 200ms, SSO integration in dev.
4) Decision checkpoint: Jul 13 for quote submission to stay on track for PO before trial end (proposed trial end: Jul 22). If PO timing slips, we'll pause billing until the PO effective date - please confirm preference in reply.

I've attached the quote and the trial checklist for your review. If you'd like, I can also open a DocuSign envelope and we can sign the SOW/Order Form electronically.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
